transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it, thanks for sharing that — that’s really common.  

Those intake calls that hit voicemail after hours… do people usually leave a message, or do they just call the next place?
User: Most leave a message, but about 70% would book if someone answered directly.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — when a live person answers, people commit on the spot.  

So roughly how many of those after‑hours intake calls are you seeing in a typical week that end up in voicemail?
User: About 12 missed calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: Got it, so around 12 a week are hitting voicemail after hours, and most of those could’ve been booked if someone picked up.  

Just so I understand the impact—if you turned even half of those into actual appointments, what would that mean for your business each month?
User: It could mean an additional intake value of around $4,320 monthly if half were converted.
Agent: That’s really clear, thank you—so we’re talking over four grand a month just from catching half of what’s currently going to voicemail.  

So I don’t assume… what kind of business are you running—law firm, home services, medical, or something else?
User: We’re a personal injury law firm.
Agent: Got it, a personal injury firm—that makes those missed after‑hours intakes even more expensive.  

When someone calls after an accident, hits your voicemail, and doesn’t book, do you feel like they usually end up signing with another firm, or is it more hit‑or‑miss?
User: They often end up signing with another firm if they don't get an immediate response.
Agent: Yeah, that tracks for PI—if you’re not first, you’re usually out.  

Given how much is at stake, are you looking for a way to actually have those after‑hours calls answered and screened right away, or are you still just exploring what’s out there?
User: We're exploring options for after-hours call answering and screening to improve our client intake process.
Agent: Makes sense, you’re right in the sweet spot for fixing this.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through the math of what those missed, after‑hours PI intakes are costing you in lost cases each month?
User: No, we haven't had a detailed walkthrough of the costs for missed after-hours personal injury intakes yet.
Agent: Gotcha, that tracks with most PI firms I talk to.  

Mind if we do a quick, simple version together now—just using your numbers—to see what’s leaking out every month?
User: Sure, let's do a quick calculation using our numbers to see potential monthly losses.
Agent: Right, based on what you shared, you’re leaking roughly $9,300 a month just from those after‑hours calls that hit voicemail and don’t convert.  

So… with that kind of money on the line, would you be open to a 20‑minute walkthrough this week where we show you exactly how to stop losing those after‑hours PI intakes?
User: Yes, I'm interested in a walkthrough this week to stop losing those after-hours personal injury intakes.
Agent: Nice, that makes a lot of sense.  

First thing so I know who I’m talking to—what’s your first name?
User: I prefer to be referred to as a partner at Bell & Associates Legal.
Agent: Got it, I’ll call you Partner, and I’ve got Bell & Associates Legal noted.  

And is the number you’re calling from right now the best number for us to text your walkthrough confirmation to?
User: No, please text the confirmation to +19172120001, that's my best contact number.
Agent: Perfect, I’ve got that number noted, thanks.  

One moment while I check availability—would you prefer the walkthrough later today or tomorrow?
Agent: Got it, thanks.  

For the walkthrough, would you rather do later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better for me.
Agent: Perfect, tomorrow works.  

I can get you in tomorrow at either 12:30 or 1:15 in the afternoon Eastern—what’s better for you?
User: 1:15 in the afternoon Eastern works for me. Book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on the calendar for you.
Agent: Perfect, you’re all set, Partner — you’re booked for tomorrow at 1:15 in the afternoon Eastern with Jay for your 20‑minute walkthrough. You’ll get a text confirmation shortly with all the details and a link in case you need to reschedule.

Is there anything else you need from me before we wrap up?

Really glad you called in today. Jay’s looking forward to meeting you tomorrow. Have a great rest of your day — bye for now!
